findings.title: Order list lazy-loads items per order and products per item (N+1)
findings.workload: Every signed-in user opening the order list (hot; polled every 30 s by web/src/orders/List.tsx:55)
findings.scale_driver: N = orders per page (max 100); M = items per order (uncapped)
findings.cost_model: 1 + N + N × M data queries: one for orders, N for items, N × M for lazy-loaded products; excludes fixed request overhead
findings.request: 1. The requested tenant page contains N=100 orders, each with M=20 items referencing distinct products; relation caches are empty. 2. GET /api/orders?page=<n>&page_size=100
findings.contrast: GET /api/orders/<id> prefetches items and their products at app/orders/views.py:61
findings.impact: Expected (B-01): constant data queries. Actual: 1 + 100 + 100 × 20 = 2101 data queries per page, growing with uncapped items per order even at a fixed page size; response latency was not measured
findings.fix: Prefetch items and their products on the list queryset at app/orders/views.py:18
findings.regression_test: After prefetching, GET /api/orders data-query counts are equal for (N,M)=(1,1), (50,1), (1,20), (50,20); each response still contains all expected orders, items and products

validation.evidence: views.py:18 fetches orders without prefetch; serializers.py:42 evaluates order.items.all() once per order and reads item.product once per item without select_related or a shared product cache

findings.title: Product list calls the pricing service once per product
findings.workload: Every visitor opening the product list (hot)
findings.cost_model: 1 + N outbound HTTP calls to the pricing service, in series
findings.request: 1. A catalogue page with N=100 products. 2. GET /api/products?page=<n>&page_size=100
findings.contrast: GET /api/products/<id> reads prices from the batch endpoint at app/products/views.py:58
findings.impact: Expected (B-05): one batched pricing call per page. Actual: 100 sequential calls per page; latency was not measured
findings.fix: Call the batch pricing endpoint once per page at app/products/views.py:31
findings.regression_test: GET /api/products issues one pricing call for page sizes 1 and 100

validation.evidence: app/products/views.py:31 calls pricing.get(product.id) inside the loop over the page

findings.title: Order export reads every order into memory without a limit
findings.workload: Tenant admins exporting orders (warm; a few times a day)
findings.cost_model: Memory proportional to all orders of the tenant; one query returning every row
findings.request: 1. A tenant with a large order history. 2. GET /api/orders/export
findings.impact: Expected (B-04): bounded memory per request. Actual: whole history materialised as a list, then as one CSV string; matters above roughly 100k orders per tenant
findings.fix: Stream rows with a server-side cursor and write the CSV incrementally to the response
findings.regression_test: Export of 10k synthetic orders keeps peak allocation below a fixed bound

validation.evidence: export.py:27 materialises every order; the route was not traced

findings.title: Dashboard widgets appear to query once per widget (N+1)
findings.workload: Tenant dashboard (warm; opened a few times per session)
findings.request: 1. A dashboard with W=12 widgets. 2. GET /api/dashboard
findings.impact: Expected (B-01): constant data queries. Suspected: one query per widget
findings.fix: None needed: the widget queries are already prefetched
findings.regression_test: Query count for GET /api/dashboard is equal for W=1 and W=12

validation.evidence: widgets.py:31 reads per-widget data; whether it is prefetched was not traced

findings.title: Product search filters on a column with no index
findings.scale_driver: Products per tenant (matters above roughly 100k products; production volume unknown)
findings.cost_model: Full scan of the products table per search
findings.request: 1. A tenant with a large product catalogue (matters above roughly 100k products; production volume unknown). 2. GET /admin/products?sku=<sku>
findings.impact: Expected: indexed lookup. Actual: db/migrations defines no index on (tenant_id, sku); the deployed schema was not observed
findings.fix: Add a composite index on (tenant_id, sku)
findings.regression_test: EXPLAIN for the search query uses the new index
